AI labels on Facebook, Threads, LinkedIn, X and YouTube: why they appear

The same photo can get an “AI info” label on Facebook, a CR icon on LinkedIn and an “altered or synthetic” note on YouTube. Most of these labels start with the same thing: metadata inside your file. Here is how each network decides, and what you can check before posting.

Updated 2026-11-18 · 5 min read
Clean your files in secondsFree, no sign-up, and everything runs in your browser — nothing is uploaded.
Open IA Cleaner

What each network looks at

  • Facebook and Threads (Meta): the same system as Instagram — the “AI info” label appears when the file carries C2PA Content Credentials or IPTC fields saying it was made or edited with AI, or when you mark it yourself. See the Instagram guide.
  • LinkedIn: shows a small CR icon on images with Content Credentials. Clicking it reveals the tool, and often that AI was used.
  • YouTube: asks creators to disclose realistic altered or synthetic content, and also uses C2PA, for example to show “captured with a camera”.
  • X and others: labelling rules change often; many rely on what the creator declares, on metadata or on their own detection.

Check and clean your file before posting

  1. Open IA Cleaner → Images (or Video for MP4/MOV).
  2. Drop the exact file you were going to upload.
  3. Look for C2PA / Content Credentials, XMP with DigitalSourceType and the box What the original reveals.
  4. Download the clean copy and upload that one.

What this won’t change

  • A label you added yourself, or one a network applies because of its own detection or your account settings.
  • Invisible watermarks in the pixels (such as SynthID) or visible logos.
  • Your obligations: most networks require you to disclose realistic AI-generated content. Removing metadata is about privacy and accuracy — for example when a small AI retouch marks a real photo as “AI” — not about hiding synthetic media.
